traffic_stub.label: Stub still takes highway traffic
traffic_stub.what: A stub of 16 m or less touching a major road, with the same traffic class (3 or higher) as that road. It still passes the AADT join, usually because it runs nearly along the highway (a slip lane or turn pocket).
traffic_stub.next: Check the segment against imagery; if it is a driveway or pocket, set its traffic class to 1 or tighten the join.

stub_access.label: Stub carries highway-level access
stub_access.what: A minor stub of 12.5 m or less touching a major road, with an access class of 3 or higher and more than twice the residents routed over any minor street it touches. The OD join (export_protect_va.py) tests short streets the same way the detour join did before the Oct. 30 fix, so some of these may hold the highway's routed residents.
stub_access.next: Apply the export_slr.py midpoint test to export_protect_va.build_update and re-export OD (no re-route needed).

major_low_traffic.label: Major road at the lowest traffic class
major_low_traffic.what: A trunk, primary, or secondary segment matched to a StreetLight value low enough for traffic class 1.
major_low_traffic.next: Check the matched StreetLight zone (aadt_zone_name); the match may be a parallel local street.

spike.label: Top quarter, every neighbor below the median
spike.what: A top-quarter segment whose every touching segment sits below the 50th percentile. Criticality should change gradually along a route, so a lone bright block often means a gap or bad link in the network.
spike.next: Look at the detour around it: a missing connection nearby can inflate one block's detour.

shape_doubles_back.label: Line doubles back on itself
shape_doubles_back.what: The segment's line turns back more than 150 degrees between two legs of 10 m or more, usually retracing a neighbor: most of these lie partly on top of other segments. The road does not do this; the line was built wrong in Streets_Network_Tahoe. The length is overstated, the map draws a spike, and joins that test overlap can miss (Mount Rose Highway 3744 scored zero traffic until Oct. 30).
shape_doubles_back.next: Rebuild these lines from the Overture segment geometry (segment_id) in the base network, then rerun the build.

parallel_split.label: Parallel pair scored far apart
parallel_split.what: Two segments sharing both endpoints (a frontage road, loop, or split carriageway) whose percentiles differ by more than 25 points. Usually expected: the highway carries the traffic and the loop does not.

unnamed_major.label: Major road with no name
unnamed_major.what: A trunk, primary, secondary, or tertiary segment with no street name in Overture. The score is fine; the label is missing on the map and in exports.
unnamed_major.next: Fill the name from the touching segments of the same class.

unknown_top.label: Unknown road class in the top quarter
unknown_top.what: A segment Overture leaves unclassified ('unknown') that ranks in the top quarter.

no_geometry.label: Scored but missing from the map
no_geometry.what: In roads_criticality.json but not in roads_geometry.geojson, so the segment is scored but never drawn.
no_geometry.next: Check publish_results.py's street read for the dropped rows.

low_use_capped.label: Detour capped: road almost nobody uses
low_use_capped.what: A minor road with a long detour but traffic class 1 and fewer than 10 residents routed. Its detour class was capped at 1 on Oct. 30 (detour_low_use). Mostly forest and seasonal roads.
low_use_capped.next: Confirm on the ground: some may be fire or evacuation access that the routing does not model.

equity_only_top.label: Top quarter from equity alone
equity_only_top.what: Traffic, detour, and access are all at the lowest class; the neighborhood equity counts alone lift the segment past the top-quarter cut.
equity_only_top.next: A weighting decision, not an error: see the note on relative quarters.

one_step_top.label: Top quarter from one step on one input
one_step_top.what: A minor street whose traffic, detour, and access classes sum to 4: one input is one class above the lowest. With 70 percent of segments at the floor, that is enough to reach the top quarter.
one_step_top.next: A classification decision, not an error: see the note on relative quarters.
